analysis:
This file is an offline Python unittest for the CI workflows (scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py). It does not touch provider runtime code, WebSocket contracts, attestation, keys, or the encrypted prefix cache (T-041). I found no direct regression against the threat-model assets or boundaries.

Changes visible in the supplied head text:
- VALIDATE_GIT (lines 152-175) tightens the check on a restored .git cache. It rejects a symlink, a non-directory, any hook other than git's .sample files, config setting core.fsmonitor, core.hooksPath or include/includeIf, and a failed git fsck. This hardens CI against code execution from a poisoned cache. The test only pins the script text.
- CACHE_GATE_STEP and CACHE_GATE (lines 176-196) skip Actions cache steps on a Darkbloom runner that has no DARKBLOOM_CACHE_URL. This prevents falling back to GitHub's own cache. The gated() helper is applied to restore and save conditions at lines 675 and 679.
- The save-cache policy stays tied to push events on master and dev, plus dispatch on dev. Pull requests never save, so pull-request code cannot poison caches that later runs restore.
- The prompt-fixture and audio caches are keyed by manifest content hash with no restore-keys, so only an exact key restores.

The test code itself is benign. It runs local subprocesses with stub swift binaries in temporary directories and shell snippets taken from the repository's own workflow text. These are trusted repo inputs.

Remaining unverified contracts, which sit outside the supplied evidence:
- The actual workflow YAML (provider-tests.yml, ci-master.yml, provider-plan.yml) was not supplied, so I could not confirm the workflows implement the pinned CACHE_GATE and VALIDATE_GIT behavior.
- The case-insensitive find patterns and the git config --file check have not been exercised for bypasses such as a hooks path set through other config keys. This is CI hardening, not a provider threat-model item.
- The hunk beyond line 879 (changed ranges up to about line 1407) was not supplied, so it is not covered by this review.
